body: ### All Submissions: - [x] Have you followed the guidelines stated in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/reflex-dev/reflex/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) file? - [x] Have you checked to ensure there aren't any other open [Pull Requests](https://github.com/reflex-dev/reflex/pulls) for the desired changed? ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) ### Changes To Core Features: - [x] Have you added an explanation of what your changes do and why you'd like us to include them? - [x] Have you written new tests for your core changes, as applicable? - [x] Have you successfully ran tests with your changes locally? ## What goes wrong `ArraySliceOperation._cached_var_name` renders a negative-step slice as the reversed forward slice `[end + 1 : start + 1]`. It has two bugs. 1. **Index `-1` wraps to `0`.** With `start == -1`, `start + 1` is `0`, so `State.items[-1::-1]` and `State.items[-1:-4:-1]` render `.slice(x, 0)` and evaluate to `[]`. Python gives the reversed list and `[5, 4, 3]`. With `end == -1`, `end + 1` is `0`, so `items[:-1:-1]` renders the whole list reversed where Python gives `[]`. String Vars go through the same code (`"hello"[-1::-1]` renders `""`). 2. **A Var step recurses forever.** The Var-step branch reads `self.step`, but the field is named `_step`. The attribute lookup falls through `Var.__getattr__` to `_cached_var_name` again, so `State.items[1:4:State.step]` raises `RecursionError` when it's rendered. ## Fix - Compute the reverse bounds once, mapping `-1` to the array length instead of `0`. An int bound is mapped statically. A Var bound gets `(bound === -1 ? arr.length : bound + 1)`. The reverse bounds are built only for a negative or Var step, so the positive-step path does no extra work. - Use the local `step` in the Var-step expression, and wrap the Var-step conditional in parentheses so that a following operation (e.g. `.length()`) applies to both branches. - For every other bound, the generated JS is unchanged. For example, the existing `[::-1]` assertion in `test_index_operation` still holds. ## Tests - `tests/units/test_var.py::test_slice_with_var_step` pins the Var-step expression. - `tests/units/test_var.py::test_var_step_slice_length_covers_both_branches` checks that `.length()` works for both step signs (Node). - `tests/units/test_var.py::test_negative_step_slices_match_python[step_var-bounds_var]` evaluates the generated JS in Node, which the test skips if Node isn't installed. It covers 9 negative-step slices (`[::-1]`, `[-1::-1]`, `[-1:-4:-1]`, `[:-1:-1]`, `[3::-1]`, `[4:0:-2]`, `[-2::-1]`, `[:-3:-1]`, `[-1::-2]`), each with every combination of int or Var step and int or Var bounds. It asserts every result equals Python's `items[s]`. - All of these fail on `main` (`fe2a78f4`): the int case gets `[]` instead of `[5, 4, 3, 2, 1]`, and the Var cases raise `RecursionError`. They pass with the fix. Checks, all run locally: - `uv run pytest tests/units`: 9849 passed. - `pre-commit run --from-ref HEAD~1 --to-ref HEAD`: ruff-format, ruff-check, codespell, update-pyi-files, pyright and ty all pass. - A news fragment is added under `packages/reflex-base/news/`. AI disclosure: an AI agent (Claude) found this bug and wrote the patch and tests, operating the `breken-ai` account. I reviewed the diff adversarially before opening this PR. I'll respond to review feedback, including Greptile/Copilot.
title: fix: negative-step Var slices at -1 and slices with a Var step
